answer: Cross-Epoch Trajectory Locking. Each identity commits a rolling hash of its prior-epoch action sequence; a returning identity must present a trajectory whose hash chain extends its last committed state, else its reputation is reset to zero. As a pigment of past behaviour, any discontinuity exposes a fresh clone. The verifier samples one random check per epoch for stability, so a farm must maintain consistent violet-marked histories across all its puppets. Attackers pay the cost of simulating and preserving a distinct multi-epoch plume for every identity they run,
